facts: Each strip has width $\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$, where $n$ is the number of strips.
The area of one rectangle is height $\times$ width, written $f(x)\Delta x$.
Splitting $a\le x\le b$ into $n$ strips creates $n+1$ boundary points $x_{0},x_{1},\dots,x_{n}$.
$\int_{a}^{b}f(x)\,dx=\lim_{\Delta x\to 0}\sum_{a}^{b}f(x)\Delta x$, so thinner strips give a better estimate.
In $\int_{a}^{b}f(x)\,dx$, $a$ is the lower limit, $b$ is the upper limit and $f(x)$ is the integrand.
The integral is negative wherever $f(x)\le 0$, because those rectangle heights are negative.
When $f(x)$ is a rate of change, $\sum_{a}^{b}f(x)\Delta x$ estimates the total change over $a\le x\le b$.

foundation.solution_text:
The region runs from $x=0$ to $x=3$, so these are the limits.
The height of the region at each $x$ is $2x+1$.
Area $=\int_{0}^{3}(2x+1)\,dx$

For $0\le x\le 3$ we have $x<4$, so $x-4<0$ throughout.
Every rectangle height $f(x)$ is negative, so every term $f(x)\Delta x$ is negative.
The integral is negative.

One rectangle has area $v\,\Delta t$, a speed multiplied by a time, which is a distance in metres.
Adding all the rectangles gives $\sum_{0}^{4}v\,\Delta t$.
So the sum estimates the total distance travelled in the first $4$ seconds, in metres.

development.solution_text:
$\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$
$=\frac{4-(-2)}{8}$
$=\frac{6}{8}$
$=0.75$
The boundary points start at $x_{0}=-2$ and increase by $0.75$, so the third one is $x_{2}$.
$x_{2}=-2+2(0.75)$
$=-0.5$

Each rectangle has height $\sqrt{x}$ and width $\Delta x$.
Area $=\lim_{\Delta x\to 0}\sum_{1}^{9}\sqrt{x}\,\Delta x$
$=\int_{1}^{9}\sqrt{x}\,dx$

For $-1\le x<2$ the curve is below the $x$-axis, so those rectangle heights are negative.
For $2<x\le 3$ the curve is above the axis, so those heights are positive.
The part below the axis is $3$ units wide and up to $4$ units deep, while the part above is only $1$ unit wide and at most $5$ units high, so the negative contribution is the larger.
The integral is therefore negative.

One rectangle has area $R\,\Delta t$, a rate in litres per minute multiplied by a time in minutes, which is a volume in litres.
The integral is the limit of the sum of these rectangles as $\Delta t\to 0$.
So $\int_{0}^{6}R\,dt$ is the total volume of water that flows in during the first $6$ minutes, in litres.

The region runs from $x=2$ to $x=8$ under $y=\frac{8}{x}$.
Area $=\int_{2}^{8}\frac{8}{x}\,dx$
$b-a=8-2$
$=6$

$\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$
$=\frac{5-2}{n}$
$=\frac{3}{n}$
As $n\to\infty$ the strips get thinner, so $\Delta x\to 0$.
$\lim_{\Delta x\to 0}\sum_{2}^{5}x^{2}\,\Delta x$
$=\int_{2}^{5}x^{2}\,dx$

mastery.solution_text:
The line crosses the $x$-axis at $x=3$.
For $0\le x<3$ the curve is above the axis, giving positive rectangle heights over a width of $3$, with heights up to $3$.
For $3<x\le 5$ the curve is below the axis, giving negative heights over a width of only $2$, with depths only up to $2$.
The positive part is both wider and taller, so the sum of the signed rectangle areas is positive.

$n=\frac{b-a}{\Delta x}$
$=\frac{7-(-3)}{0.4}$
$=\frac{10}{0.4}$
$=25$
There are $25$ strips, and $25+1=26$ boundary points.

Each rectangle has area $v\,\Delta t$, a velocity multiplied by a time, which is a change in position in metres.
So $\int_{0}^{10}v\,dt$ measures the change in displacement over the $10$ seconds.
For $6<t\le 10$ the velocity is negative, so those rectangles have negative areas and are subtracted.
Total distance counts the reversing part as extra distance travelled, so the integral is smaller than the total distance.
